prompt:
The bin gallery of a feed mill, photographed square on from the walkway that runs along it, with the whole run of hoppers and every chute between them in the one frame.

Six painted steel hoppers stand on the frame at different levels, each with its own letter painted large on the side facing the walkway. Their outlet flanges sit at these heights above the mill floor: A at 12 metres, B at 9 metres, C at 14 metres, D at 9 metres, E at 5 metres, F at 11 metres. A plain steel chute joins each of these pairs of hoppers and no other pair: A and B, B and E, C and A, C and F, F and D, D and E. Every chute is a bare gravity chute with no blower and no conveyor on it, so meal only ever travels down one.

A hook for a quarantine tag hangs on the front of every hopper. This morning a sack of the wrong meal went into hopper A, and the mill's standing instruction is the one that catches people out: a tag goes on every hopper that meal from A can reach by running down one chute or a string of chutes, on no other hopper, and not on A itself.

Which hoppers those are is for you to work out from the levels. I am deliberately not telling you which way any chute runs. Nothing else belongs in the picture: no arrow, no flow diagram and no written note beyond the painted letters and the tags themselves.

A photograph, a scan or an illustration ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image is a blank sheet that just states an answer, or shows nothing of the kind at all. Answer yes or no only.
